entries.title: Reasons for purchase
entries.label: 08-Buying Motivations
entries.text: Reasons for purchase Purchase drivers depth analysis Functional drivers Driver I: Turn data into end-to-end business stream --- Clients are usually not “no software”, but rather too many software, forms and chat tools. The real purchase objective is to reduce duplicate entries and allow sales, procurement, warehousing, finance and management to work around the same data. Corresponding product values: harmonized data model, cross-module trigger, API/database connection, business questions. Driver II: Rapid adaptation to non-standardized processes --- The systems and operations of growing enterprises are still changing, and the traditional ERP two is slow and expensive, and the purely standard cloud service is not very relevant. Visualization brings not “development for all” as a core value, but rather a change in business that does not wait in line for IT. Corresponding product values: forms, processes, reports, portals, templates and custom operations. Driver III: Let AI move from "response to questions" to "implementation" --- Businesses ' new sense of universal chat robots has declined and are more willing to pay for automatic filing, filling, generating quotations, triggering approvals, forecasting inventories and synchronizing assignments. Corresponding product value: Job intelligence, AI CRM, procurement request price, meeting to-do, cross-system implementation. Driver IV: Security and control --- Conference, client, contractual, financial and personnel data are sensitive. Privatization deployments, competencies, logs and enterprise-owned servers will significantly increase the willingness to monitor clients ' payments. Corresponding product values: privatization, enterprise-level security, data segregation, logs, letter creation and certification. Driver V: Cross-regional collaboration with weak networks --- For cross-border trade, overseas branches, factories and remote service teams, multilingual, real-time captioning, standardized documentation and low-bandwidth meetings are business continuity requirements rather than mere optimization. entries.title: CRM Industry Core Conclusions
entries.label: 01-Industry Core Conclusions
entries.text: CRM Industry Core Conclusions Dimension Current knowledge --- --- Industry role CRM is the system of record for customer identity, relationships, marketing, sales, service, channel collaboration and revenue analysis. It is broader than a contact directory or a lead list. Best-fit demand High-value B2B sales with long cycles, repeated follow-up, complex quotations and a need to connect ERP, finance or order data. Priority segments Export manufacturing, industrial distribution and cross-border B2B are the first priority segments; B2B software/services and international logistics are secondary segments. Market stage CRM is moving from customer records and sales-process digitisation toward unified data, AI-assisted decisions and AI-executed workflows. Data boundary Industry economic indicators are proxy indicators for the customer pool, not CRM SaaS TAM. CRM, CRM SaaS and sales-force-automation figures use different statistical scopes. Compliance baseline Customer data, marketing outreach, profiling, AI-generated content and cross-border transfers require purpose limitation, permissions, consent or another lawful basis, auditability and user controls. Durable opportunity Industry workflows, AI execution, quotation/order/collection linkage, data quality, compliant cross-border outreach and low-complexity deployment are more defensible than an AI label alone. --- Source - 01-source-files/kuailu-global-v1/industry-materials/Industry Research Report - CRM and HR.md - https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202602/t20260228 1962661.html

entries.label: 09-Laws & Compliance
entries.text: CRM Laws & Compliance Requirements Jurisdiction Requirement relevant to CRM operations --- --- Mainland China PIPL requires a lawful basis, purpose limitation and appropriate protection for customer and contact data. Automated marketing should offer a non-personalised option or a convenient refusal mechanism. Mainland China Network data rules require safeguards such as encryption, backup, access control and security authentication. Mainland China Cross-border transfers need a separate assessment. Data that contains personal information cannot be treated as ordinary enterprise data, even when used for international trade. European Union GDPR requires a lawful basis, transparency, data-subject rights, retention controls and safeguards for profiling or significant automated decisions. United States CAN-SPAM requires accurate sender information, a physical postal address and a clear, working opt-out mechanism for commercial email. AI-generated voice outreach may also trigger TCPA requirements. Singapore and ASEAN PDPA and the Do Not Call Registry affect collection, use, disclosure and marketing outreach. ASEAN AI guidance supports a common responsible-AI baseline but does not replace national laws. Product control Maintain consent/lawful-basis tags, source records, suppression lists, regional rules, export logs, retention settings and human approval for high-risk actions. --- Source - 01-source-files/kuailu-global-v1/industry-materials/Industry Research Report - CRM and HR.md - https://www.cac.gov.cn/2021-08/20/c 1631050028355286.htm - https://www.cac.gov.cn/2024-03/22/c 1712776611775634.htm - https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business - https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa - https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/about/the-legislation/pdpa-overview

entries.title: HR Laws & Compliance Requirements
entries.label: 09-Laws & Compliance
entries.text: HR Laws & Compliance Requirements Jurisdiction Requirement relevant to HR operations --- --- Mainland China PIPL requires a lawful basis and appropriate protection for employee information. HR processing under labour rules or collective agreements must still follow necessity, transparency and security duties. Mainland China Significant automated HR decisions require fairness, explanation and a human review or appeal path. AI screening should assist rather than silently determine hiring outcomes. Mainland China The 2024 cross-border data rules provide a conditional HR-management route for certain employee transfers, but do not remove other PIPL obligations. Mainland China Face-recognition rules effective 1 June 2025 emphasise necessity and minimisation; non-biometric attendance options should remain available where they can achieve the same purpose. Mainland China Personal-information compliance audits effective 1 May 2025 make data maps, access history and audit exports valuable for larger processors. Labour, social-insurance, tax, wage and working-time rules require regional and effective-date versioning. European Union GDPR and the EU AI Act treat employment and recruitment AI as a high-governance area; maintain data governance, logs, technical documentation and human oversight ahead of the relevant 2027 high-risk obligations. United States Federal rules are supplemented by anti-discrimination enforcement and local requirements such as New York City’s automated employment decision-tool rules. Singapore and ASEAN PDPA and regional responsible-AI guidance support privacy, accountability and explainability; country-specific employment and data requirements still apply. --- Source - 01-source-files/kuailu-global-v1/industry-materials/Industry Research Report - CRM and HR.md - https://www.cac.gov.cn/2021-08/20/c 1631050028355286.htm - https://www.cac.gov.cn/2024-03/22/c 1712776611775634.htm - https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-03/21/c 1744174262156096.htm - https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai - https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/about/the-legislation/pdpa-overview

entries.text: HR Industry Risks Risk Business impact Control direction --- --- --- AI hiring bias or opaque scoring Unfair exclusion, disputes and regulatory exposure. entries.title: HR Industry Adoption & Implementation Considerations
entries.label: 14-Commercialisation & GTM
entries.text: HR Industry Adoption & Implementation Considerations Consideration Industry-level guidance --- --- Workforce pattern Multi-site, high-turnover, non-standard-hour and attendance-driven payroll operations usually have the strongest automation need. Evaluation metrics Compare HR processing hours, payroll error rate, onboarding time, attendance exceptions and reconciliation effort against a defined baseline. Rule governance Version regional wage, overtime, tax and social-insurance rules by effective date; record approvals before payroll closing. Data readiness Reconcile employee, organisation, position, site, contract and payroll masters before automation. Rollout model Start with one site or business unit, validate attendance and payroll reconciliation, then extend to more sites and countries. Evidence quality Separate audited outcomes, research estimates, supplier claims and internal measurements; do not generalise one customer result. --- Source - 01-source-files/kuailu-global-v1/industry-materials/Industry Research Report - CRM and HR.md
